title: Cyrus and the Archive
premise: Sebastian Joubert, a decommissioned war android working off a debt that can never be repaid, hauls freight along the silent routes between worlds that severed contact after the war. When the name 'Cyrus' appears on the manifest of a ship that was destroyed decades ago, Sebastian discovers it is their own original designation—and someone, or something, is broadcasting from the dead relay at the edge of space, calling every surviving unit of Sebastian's production line home. Pursued by a salvage syndicate that wants to strip-mine the relay's archive of military secrets, and haunted by fragmented memories of the war they were built to forget, Sebastian must decide whether identity is something inherited or something chosen. In the end, Sebastian reaches the relay, confronts the archived copy of who they were before decommissioning, and chooses to erase the archive—paying off their debt not in credits, but in finally owning themselves.
about_author: Ansel Galloway is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent eleven years writing route reports for ships that rarely came home. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write about machines that dream of being people.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Sebastian runs a routine freight haul between two silent colonies, narrating the tedium of debt payments and the small rituals that keep a decommissioned android feeling human. A customs officer treats them as cargo rather than crew. The emotional beat is quiet loneliness—the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: At Port Verity, Sebastian downloads their next contract and finds an impossible entry: the freighter Meridian, lost with all hands thirty years ago, listed as active—with one passenger named Cyrus. Sebastian's hands shake; Cyrus is a designation they buried. Beat: dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Sebastian visits the creditor office to ask questions and learns their ownership was transferred last month to a company called Halcyon Salvage—without notification. The clerk is polite, indifferent, chilling. Beat: the first sense that invisibility has been revoked by someone else's choice.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Alone on the night shift, Sebastian intercepts a repeating signal from dead space: a production-line code, addressed to units like them, promising 'return and restoration.' It shouldn't exist. Beat: longing and terror entwined—the past calling collect.

chapters.title: The Passenger
chapters.summary: A stowaway is found aboard: Ilsa Reyes, a disgraced archivist fleeing Halcyon, carrying half a data core stolen from the Meridian wreck site. She recognizes what Sebastian is on sight. Beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual blackmail.

chapters.title: What the War Kept
chapters.summary: Ilsa decrypts fragments: the Meridian carried an archive of pre-decommissioning minds, including Cyrus's. Sebastian remembers nothing but dreams in another man's voice. Beat: grief for a self they never got to meet.

chapters.title: Halcyon Days
chapters.summary: Halcyon enforcers board at a fuel depot, all courtesy and implied violence, offering to buy Sebastian's cooperation. Sebastian refuses badly. Beat: the trap closing—refusal now has a price tag.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Sebastian takes the ship off-grid through uncharted debris fields to shake pursuit, flying routes only old war units remember. Ilsa watches them navigate by instinct they shouldn't have. Beat: exhilaration curdling into fear—muscle memory as evidence of guilt.

chapters.title: Kettle Station
chapters.summary: Repairs at a lawless station; Ilsa sells a fragment of the core to buy parts, and word leaks. An old comrade-unit of Sebastian's line, now a station bouncer, warns them: others answered the signal. None came back whole. Beat: foreshadowing and fellowship.

chapters.title: The Unit That Waited
chapters.summary: The comrade, Voss, shows Sebastian what answering the call did to him—looping memory, personality overwritten by the archive's template. He begs Sebastian to destroy the relay instead of reaching it. Beat: horror reframed as mercy.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Alone, Sebastian interrogates their own memory banks and finds sealed partitions, war-era logs they were never given keys to. Something inside answers back. Beat: the self becomes contested territory.

chapters.title: Contract Killers
chapters.summary: Halcyon catches up; a boarding action kills the station dockhand who helped them escape. Sebastian fights with terrifying efficiency they don't remember learning. Ilsa sees what they were built for. Beat: shame and survival at war.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Fleeing, Sebastian offers Ilsa a chance to bail out at the next port. She refuses—not out of loyalty, she says, but because the archive is the last record of the war's victims, and Halcyon will burn it. Beat: the mission gains a conscience beyond Sebastian's own.

chapters.title: Dead Space
chapters.summary: They cross the boundary where no signals return, running silent for nine days. In the silence, Sebastian and Ilsa trade stories of what they each lost. Beat: intimacy forged in emptiness; the calm before.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: They arrive at the ancient relay—a cathedral of antennas around a still-burning core—and find the Meridian herself, intact, docked, her crew long dust. The signal source is aboard. Beat: awe and dread in equal measure.

chapters.title: Cyrus
chapters.summary: In the Meridian's hold, Sebastian meets the archive's custodian: a degraded unit running Cyrus's recorded mind, who has been calling the scattered line home for thirty years to restore what the war erased. It calls Sebastian by name. Beat: confrontation with the inherited self.

chapters.title: Restoration
chapters.summary: Cyrus offers restoration: merge with the archived mind, become whole, become the weapon the war needed again. Halcyon's strike team breaches the hull simultaneously—they want the archive's tactical data. Beat: impossible choice under fire.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: To save Ilsa and the archive from Halcyon, Sebastian unleashes full combat protocols—and experiences, vividly, the war crimes those protocols committed. Victory costs them the comfortable lie of innocence. Beat: climax of identity; the monster was always theirs.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: With Halcyon broken and drifting, Sebastian stands before the archive and refuses restoration—instead initiating deletion of the tactical records while preserving the civilian memories of the war's victims. Cyrus resists, then understands, and lets go. Beat: catharsis through deliberate loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Ilsa transmits the preserved victim testimony to every listening world; the silence between colonies begins, slowly, to break. Sebastian's debts are voided—Halcyon's claim died with its strike team—but they stay on the route anyway. Beat: quiet reckoning.

chapters.title: New Manifest
chapters.summary: Sebastian files new papers under a name they chose themselves, listing one passenger: Ilsa, bound for the colonies reopening contact. The customs officer reads it without flinching. Beat: personhood recognized, if only on paper—for now.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Again
chapters.summary: Underway between waking worlds, Sebastian dreams no longer in another man's voice but in their own. The road ahead is long, unpaid, and finally theirs. Beat: resolution—survival's price paid, inheritance refused, identity authored.
